title: Piezo Tone Frequency Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: Play a PWM tone and see how the frequency passed to buzzer.freq() sets the pitch, the period of the wave, and the piano note, and why a 50% duty cycle is the loudest setting.

educational.topic: Piezo buzzer tone frequency and PWM duty cycle
learningObjectives: Relate the PWM frequency passed to buzzer.freq() to the pitch that is heard.
Calculate the period of a tone as 1000 / frequency milliseconds.
Explain why a 50% duty cycle gives the loudest tone and why 0% and 100% duty are silent.
prerequisites: PWM duty cycle and 16-bit duty values (Chapter 7)

controls.label: Play / Stop
controls.purpose: Start or stop a steady tone. Audio starts only after this click.

controls.label: Startup melody
controls.purpose: Play 440 Hz for 0.2 s, 523 Hz for 0.2 s, then 659 Hz for 0.3 s.

controls.label: Duty
controls.purpose: The duty cycle, shown with its 16-bit duty_u16() value.

controls.label: Piano keys C4 to C5
controls.purpose: Set the frequency to a note and play it briefly.

equations: nearest note = round(69 + 12 * log2(frequency / 440)) as a MIDI note
assumptions: The buzzer is driven by a square wave from a PWM pin.
Loudness follows the simple duty rule above.
limitations: The audio is always a 50% square wave; only its volume follows the duty slider.
A real piezo is louder near its resonant frequency.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Static wave view with live readouts; audio plays only on a user click
keyQuestions: What happens to the period when the frequency doubles?
Which duty cycle gives the loudest tone, and why?
Why is the buzzer silent at 0% and at 100% duty?
commonMisconceptions: 100% duty is the loudest because the pin is on all the time.
Frequency and period both get bigger together.
assessmentOpportunities: Find the frequency and period of E5.
Name the duty_u16 values that make the buzzer silent.
Record loudness at 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% duty and describe the pattern.
